name: Coffee
description: Coffee originated in Africa and was later cultivated and traded across the Arabian Peninsula before spreading to Europe and eventually becoming a global crop.

places.name: Ethiopia
places.notes: Coffee plants of the genus Coffea are native to the highlands of Ethiopia, which are widely regarded as the botanical origin of Arabica coffee.

places.name: Yemen
places.notes: Coffee was cultivated in Yemen and became associated with the development of coffee-drinking culture and early commercial coffee trade.

places.name: Arabian Peninsula
places.notes: Coffee was traded through the Arabian Peninsula and Red Sea commercial networks.

places.name: Ottoman Empire
places.notes: Coffee spread through Ottoman territories during the sixteenth century, and coffeehouses became important social institutions.

places.name: Europe
places.notes: Coffee reached European markets during the seventeenth century and gradually developed into a major commercial beverage.
